correctness.rationale: The synchronous three-color cyclic cellular automaton on loopless complete multipartite graphs K_{n1,...,nr}, r≥3 and all ni≥1, has an exact support evolution: a vertex of color c advances iff c+1 occurs in a different part. Recording multiplicities of each of seven nonempty part-color-support sets capped at two is sufficient to decide all successor tests and to reconstruct the next capped signature. The inspected source enumerates the complete 2158 realizable signatures and proves by finite exhaustive quotient that every signature after two steps is monochromatic or all-advancing; independently reimplemented signature dynamics reproduce the 1972/165/21 first-entry profile and all T⁵=T² relations, and independently simulated labelled examples reproduce periodic counts 9,21,273. Since the finite quotient is an exact factor for arbitrary part number and sizes, this is not an extrapolation from finite graph samples. All-advancing configurations rotate globally and have period exactly 3; only the 3 global monochromes are fixed. The product of onto-function counts over supports yields the complete R census, (R−3)/3 three-cycles and zeta function. The exhibited mixed-color same-part configuration proves sharpness two if any part has size≥2; singleton case sharpness one.
